evidence_set: 278 people with methamphetamine dependence were assessed in four one-month periods (baseline, 3 months, 1 year, 3 years); all were interviewed at the first three time points and 230 (83%) at 3 years, giving 1064 person-months. Psychotic symptoms were present in 25% of observed months (273 months in the Table), and 60% of participants had symptoms in at least one observed month.

Days of methamphetamine use were self-reported; hair analysis in a subsample of 83 people from the wider cohort found false reporting of abstinence in 6% of cases. Psychotic symptoms were rated by trained interviewers (agreement 93%, kappa 0.86, in 42 audiotaped interviews rated by a second interviewer); the paper does not state whether interviewers were blind to methamphetamine use.
